# Revelation 8: Research Notes for a Verse-by-Verse Commentary

**What I couldn't find:** I ran out of search and page-reading allowance before reaching any Lutheran (lcms.org, 1517.org), Pentecostal (ag.org, pneumareview.com), Orthodox (oca.org), NET Bible note or bibleodyssey.org pages on this chapter. Those views are left out. I also didn't find anything from prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teachers on Revelation 8. The "popular modern" point I did find is the Chernobyl–Wormwood idea (v. 11). Matthew Henry's and Wesley's notes on vv. 8–11 and Gill's notes on vv. 1–10 aren't in what I read. The Pulpit Commentary page I read stopped partway through vv. 8–9.

**The big question across the chapter: how do the trumpets fit with the seals?**
- **Futurist (the trumpets are still to come):** Precept Austin says the seventh seal contains the seven trumpets, and the seventh trumpet contains the seven bowls. That makes 19 judgments in all, each set getting worse. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary
- **Wesley (historicist):** He agrees the trumpets belong to the seventh seal. But he says the trumpets stretch from roughly John's day to the end of the world. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/revelation-8.html
- **Pulpit Commentary (repeating cycles):** The trumpets are a separate vision running alongside the seals. Both cover human history from start to finish, and each points in general to God's judgments. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html
- **Coffman:** The half hour of silence is the whole of the seventh seal. The seals cover the entire time between Christ's two comings. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/8-1.html
- **Utley (bible.org):** The series partly or fully repeat each other and cover the same period, a view first put forward by Victorinus of Pettau in the third century. https://bible.org/seriespage/revelation-8-9
- **D.A. Carson (The Gospel Coalition):** There's no simple lining-up of trumpets and seals, and no simple repetition. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/sermon/revelation-part-14/
- **Guzik (Enduring Word):** He sets out both the repeating and the in-order views. Because John reports from eternity, he says, the order is hard to fix; the point is that the judgments are real. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/

---

**v. 1: The silence**
- **Traditional reading:** Guzik reads the silence as sober awe before the coming judgments. Heaven is normally full of praise, so half an hour is a long time. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
- **Got Questions:** Scripture doesn't give the reason. Possible meanings are reverence before the Judge, solemn reflection, or the calm before the storm. https://www.gotquestions.org/silence-in-heaven.html
- **Precept Austin:** Points out that the Jewish temple kept silence while incense was offered. It links the silence to Zephaniah 1:7. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary
- **Literal or symbolic time?**
  - Constable thinks it is probably a literal 30 minutes. Barnes simply calls it a short period. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/8-1.html
  - Schaff's commentary reads "half an hour" as the hour of judgment being broken off. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/scn/revelation-8.html
- **Wesley:** The silence shows those around the throne waiting in deep reverence. It is "only a preparation" for the trumpets. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/revelation-8.html
- **Matthew Henry:** One option he gives is the "silence of peace": no cries of distress were rising from the church. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/8-1.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** The silence stands for the eternal rest and sabbath of heaven, which can't be described. It notes that Bede, Primasius and Victorinus took it as the start of eternal peace. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html

**v. 2: Seven angels and seven trumpets**
- **Guzik:** Jewish tradition held that seven angels stand before God. In the Old Testament, trumpets sounded the alarm for war or called God's people together. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
- **Precept Austin:**
  - It warns that naming these angels from Enoch or Tobit is speculation. It notes Gabriel "stands in the presence of God" (Luke 1:19). https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary
  - It sees the seven ram's horns at Jericho as a picture of these trumpets. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary
- **Wesley:** Trumpets proclaim God's works, by which every opposing power is shaken until the world becomes God's kingdom. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/revelation-8.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** It mentions Tobit 12:15, where Raphael is one of seven angels. Some take the seven as archangels; others identify them with the "seven Spirits." https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html

**v. 3: The angel with the golden censer — a real point of disagreement**
- **Is the angel Christ?**
  - Matthew Henry thinks it "very probable" that this is the Lord Jesus, the church's high priest. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/8-3.html
  - Chuck Smith also believes it is Jesus. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/8-3.html
  - Older sermons on Bible Hub argue that it is Christ's intercession that makes the saints' prayers acceptable. https://biblehub.com/sermons/revelation/8-3.htm
- **A created angel?**
  - Wesley says it is a created angel: in this part of Revelation, Christ is never called an angel, only the Lamb. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/8.htm
  - Precept Austin agrees. Christ already appears as the Lamb, and "another" means another of the same kind. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary
  - The Pulpit Commentary notes that Bede, Elliott, Primasius and Vitringa took the angel to be Christ. It disagrees, while affirming that Christ is our only Mediator. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html
  - Guzik sets out both views. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
- **Catholic reading:** Catholic Answers says the passage shows an angel offering the saints' prayers. So it is fitting for Catholics to rely on the prayers of those in heaven, human or angel. https://www.catholic.com/bible-navigator/intercession-of-the-saints/revelation83-4
  - The Catholic Encyclopedia cites this verse in its article on intercession. https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/08070a.htm
  - Another Catholic Answers piece links the verse to Tobit 12:15. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/online-edition/defending-the-prayers-of-the-saints
- **The altars:** The Pulpit Commentary thinks two altars are in view: fire from the altar of sacrifice, and incense burned on the golden altar. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html

**v. 4: Prayers rising like incense**
- **Clarke (quoted by Guzik):** The angel offers the incense, and the prayers rise with it. The rising smoke shows they were accepted. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
- **Pulpit Commentary:** God hears the prayers, and the trumpet judgments that follow are his answer. https://biblehub.com/revelation/8-4.htm
- **Precept Austin:** Points to Psalm 141:2 and Acts 10:4. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary

**v. 5: Fire thrown to the earth**
- **Guzik:** The prayers, touched by fire from the altar, come back to earth as judgment. He adds that God's people can hasten the Lord's coming by prayer. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
- **Precept Austin:** Fire stands for judgment (Ezekiel 10:2). There is a direct cause-and-effect link between the prayers and the judgment. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary
- **Whedon:** The fire also stands for God's purity, which cleanses believers and consumes the ungodly. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/whe/revelation-8.html

**v. 6: The angels get ready**
- **Wesley:** The prayers of the saints and the trumpets go together. Their effects may run through all seven. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/revelation-8.html
- **Pulpit Commentary:** The verses in between (vv. 3–5) show that the saints' prayers are the immediate cause of the judgments. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html

**v. 7: First trumpet — hail and fire on the land**
- **Literal or symbolic? This splits readers sharply.**
  - Guzik reads it plainly, "without escaping into a creative symbolism." But he stresses that God, not "nature," brings the judgment. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
  - Wesley reads it historically: the earth means Asia, especially Palestine, and the Jewish disasters under Hadrian. Trees are leading men and grass the common people. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/8.htm
  - Matthew Henry says commentators can't agree whether it is a storm of heresy (Arianism) or of war. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Rev/Rev_008.cfm
  - The Pulpit Commentary notes the echo of Egypt's plagues and reads it as God's judgments on the wicked in every age. It lists many proposed fulfilments, such as Gothic invasions and Trajan's wars. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html
- **What "a third" means:** Guzik says it shows mercy: God "spares more than He smites." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/

**vv. 8–9: Second trumpet — the burning mountain**
- **Guzik:** The word "like" shows it isn't an actual mountain. He prefers something like a meteor to reading it as a symbol of a nation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
- **Pulpit Commentary:** It is probably a volcano-like picture of a great judgment. It notes the guesses about Roman ships. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-8.html
- **Jamieson, Fausset & Brown:** Points out that some symbolic readers take the ships as churches. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jfu/revelation-8.html
- **Wesley:** The second trumpet strikes the Roman heathen in particular. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/8.htm

**vv. 10–11: Third trumpet — the star Wormwood**
- **Meaning of the name:** Wormwood is a bitter plant, a byword for bitterness and sorrow. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
  - Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary link it to Jeremiah 9:15 and Deuteronomy 29:18. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/8-11.htm
- **Who or what is the star?**
  - Gill reads it as bitter troubles on the provinces of the Roman Empire. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/wbt/revelation/8-11.html
  - Some take the star as a false teacher, such as Arius. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/8-11.htm
  - Guzik quotes Clarke's skeptical list (Attila, Genseric, Arius…). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
  - Got Questions reads it as a future event that will make the water poisonous. https://www.gotquestions.org/wormwood.html
- **Popular modern teaching:** Bible Hub notes the claim that "Chernobyl" roughly means "wormwood." It says this link is "not universally accepted" as the fulfilment. https://biblehub.com/q/what_event_explains_wormwood's_bitter_waters.htm

**v. 12: Fourth trumpet — sun, moon and stars darkened**
- **Guzik:** One third of the day and night goes completely dark. He links it to Matthew 24:29. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
- **Wesley:** Sun, moon and stars may stand for people overwhelmed by disaster. He thinks the first four trumpets together cover nearly 400 years. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/8.htm

**v. 13: The eagle and the three woes**
- **Eagle or angel?** The best old manuscripts (Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Vaticanus) and the Vulgate read "eagle." https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jfu/revelation-8.html
  - Whedon links it to the fourth living creature, which was like a flying eagle (4:7). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/whe/revelation-8.html
  - Precept Austin says an eagle speaking is not a sufficient reason to call it symbolic. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-8-commentary
- **What the woes mean:**
  - Guzik notes that a third of the earth's people die in the trumpets that follow. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-8/
  - Whedon says the woes are aimed at the ungodly who lack God's seal (9:4). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/whe/revelation-8.html
